newsitem.title: UK: Private stake in London tube possibility - minister.
newsitem.headline: Private stake in London tube possibility - minister.

text.p: The government has not ruled out private enterprise taking an equity stake in London Underground, Transport Minister Gavin Strang said on Wednesday.

Speaking in a parliamentary debate on the future of the "tube" system, Strang however ruled out the new Labour government following its Conservative predecessor which had been planning a full transfer out of the public sector.
"The option of wholesale privatisation is ruled out," Strang said.
He said the government was calling in consultants to look at possible ways to rescue the system from financial difficulties which were delaying much-needed repairs and improvements.

But even before they reported, he could say that one option was to use the Private Finance Initiative "in relation, for example, to the power side, a PFI which we believe has the potential to be successful".

Strang added: "There is the option, which has not been ruled out, of a private equity stake in the capital of the underground, but that would be on terms very different from what we saw under the Conservatives with their privatisation measures." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
